decisions.reason: As a visible 2018 launch built on the already accepted BASIC 518 platform, this modular trommel screen has prior market traction and too much recent investment and public commitment to reverse after only one year.

The mobile high-speed flail shredders were given their own product page and fit the firm's stated push in advanced, flexible recycling machinery, so management would likely continue rather than abandon such a fresh and visible launch.

Even with only limited website evidence, the mobile high-speed grinder matches the firm's core mobile processing business and any weak early uptake could easily be treated as a temporary market-ramp issue in 2019.

The stationary electric fine shredder supports tougher processing requirements and resource-saving solutions, making it strategically aligned enough that management would be inclined to justify and continue the recent development effort.

A mobile high-speed grinder for green waste extends the firm's established recycling and biomass offering, and after a 2018 launch management would likely interpret early uncertainty as normal commercialization rather than a reason to exit.

Because the stationary single-shaft pre-shredders were prominently presented and sit close to the firm's core shredding portfolio, the combination of sunk development costs, strategic fit, and public commitment strongly favors keeping them.
